summary: Redwood walked Nova Strata through Optimize recommendations in the Console focused on prefetch/prefix KV strategies and batching trade-offs. Primary goals: meet a 75ms P95 budget for chat-like sessions, reduce per-token cost for multi-turn sessions, and design a pilot for Dedicated vs Hosted fallback. Action items: Redwood to share cost simulation CSV and QuickBench runs; Nova to share traffic sample and SLOs. Customer concerned about encryption/KMS for KV cache and region residency.
transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): All right, hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE on this account, and with me is Carlos and June from solutions. We planned a 45-ish minute walkthrough of the Optimize tab and then a simulation using Nova Strata's latency budget.
[00:18] Aisha (Nova Strata): Thanks Maya, yeah we wanted to get concrete numbers on how prefetch and the prefix KV cache actually move the needle on cost. Our thing is we have multi-turn chat sessions that average 8 turns, some with 2–3 long vectors.
[00:34] Carlos (Redwood): Cool, we'll show the Console first — the Optimize page has a quick snapshot, then we'll dive into the cost model simulator. Important context: are you currently on any reserved capacity or fully hosted?
[00:44] Devon (Nova): We're currently on a mix — staging is on hosted API, prod is in early Dedicated eval with a single GPU pool. But, people are hitting P95 spikes around 120–150ms and we want to push P95 under 75ms.
[00:58] June (Redwood): Ok that helps. Two things to call out up front: prefetch/prefix KV cache reduces token work for repeated context, and batching reduces per-token compute cost but can add latency if you wait too long for batches. The Console lets you simulate both.
[01:20] Aisha: When you say prefetch, you mean precomputing KV for the common prompt prefixes? We've had an internal team call it "session warmup" so just checking terms.
[01:28] Carlos: Yes exactly. Prefetch = pre-computing KV cache for the static prefix so later generation only attends to new tokens. Sometimes the transcriber writes it as K V cache which is funny, but same thing. The key levers: how many prefixes you keep, TTL, and hit rate.
[01:42] Samir (Nova): Quick sec — from a security standpoint, the KV cache, is that encrypted at rest with our KMS? We cannot have PII in the cache unencrypted.
[01:50] Maya: Good question. Short answer: yes, customer-managed KMS/HSM support exists for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use our managed KMS but we have an enterprise option to bring-your-own. We'll include the KMS diagram in the docs.
[02:02] Devon: Great. Back to cost — show us a scenario where prefetch reduces tokens.
[02:06] Carlos: Sure. (shares screen) Here is the Console Optimize simulator. On the left we set traffic profile — session length distribution, turn frequency. Middle panel has model choices, batching policy (max batch wait 6ms default), and prefix cache parameters — number of prefixes, avg hit rate. On the right you get estimated throughput, token cost, and P95.
[02:28] [02:28] Carlos: I'll flip the baseline — no prefix cache, 8-turn sessions, batch wait 6ms, model x-small (a 7B variant). Baseline cost per 1k sessions is shown as $48 and P95 ~ 120ms.
[02:42] Aisha: That P95 looks like what our staging metrics show.
[02:45] Carlos: Now enable prefix cache with a 75% hit rate on the prefix and TTL 24h. That drops generated tokens by ~38% and cost per 1k sessions to $31, P95 drops to 85ms.
[02:59] Priya (Nova): Wait why does P95 drop? I thought caching mainly saved compute, not infer latency.
[03:05] Carlos: Good nuance — it reduces per-request decode work so CPU/GPU time per request drops which reduces queueing. With less queueing, the P95 improves. Also when the cache hits, we can short-circuit some attention which is faster.
[03:18] Devon: What about long-tail sessions with rare prefixes? Do we regress on P99?
[03:22] June: In the console you can model a mix: 85% sessions hit cached prefix, 15% are cold. We show both P95 and P99. Typically P99 will still be higher but overall cost is lower.
[03:36] [03:36] Carlos: Now let's toggle prefetching — proactively prefetching top-100 prefixes reduces cold-starts but increases storage and precompute cost. In this example prefetching brings P95 to 72ms and cost to $34 because you pay a bit for the precompute.
[03:54] Aisha: Hm so we might accept a small cost increase to meet the latency SLO. That's helpful.
[03:58] Maya: Exactly, that's the trade-off. The Optimize tab will surface Pareto points: min-cost configuration, latency-targeted config, and balanced config.
[04:10] Samir: For Dedicated, do we get different kernel choices that affect latency? We've seen weird perf differences with quantized vs unquantized models.
[04:18] Carlos: Yes — Dedicated lets you pin GPU hardware and kernel profiles; for instance bf16 kernel on A100 vs int8 on T4 changes throughput/latency. The optimizer includes microbenchmarks to pick kernels for your workload. We'll attach the kernel-selection doc.
[04:32] Devon: Can we run our own QuickBench on our trace? I'd like to validate P99 numbers.
[04:36] Carlos: Absolutely. QuickBench is a small harness we run — if you provide a sanitized trace (timestamped requests + prompt lengths) we can run an approximated replay on our bench infra. That's one action.
[04:46] Aisha: About data residency — we need KV cache and prefetch storage to be in EU only. Is that supported?
[04:52] Maya: Yes, with Private and Dedicated we support region-restricted caches; hosted can be pinned to region but enterprise package recommended for strict legal controls. We'll add the region mapping doc.
[05:04] [05:04] Carlos: Let's walk a specific example with your numbers. Devon, you mentioned 8-turn average, what's the typical prefix reuse ratio in those 8 turns? Do users repeat the first prompt often?
[05:14] Devon: We estimate about 60% reuse on the first two turns, and then conversation diverges.
[05:18] Carlos: Ok set hit rate 60% baseline. (inputs) Baseline cost per 10k requests is $420. With prefix cache at 60% hit, cost drops to $260 and P95 from 120ms to 88ms. If we prefetch the top 50 prefixes (hot starts) hit goes to 78%, cost $295, P95 74ms.
[05:40] Aisha: So prefetch cost increases but helps P95. Good. What about batching? If we increase batch window to 12ms to gain better batch sizes, do we blow the latency SLO?
[05:50] Carlos: There's a sweet spot. If your request arrival rate is high, increasing batch wait slightly yields better per-token cost without hurting P95 because batches fill quickly. But at lower QPS you add additional queuing delay. The console sim can use your arrival distribution to show that.
[06:06] Priya: Our production QPS is bursty — mornings are 4-5x baseline. How does the system handle bursts with cache warming?
[06:12] June: We recommend autoscaling + a warm pool of Dedicated nodes for burst windows. Also pre-warming prefixes ahead of expected spikes helps. The routing policy can fallback to a cheaper model when Dedicated pool is saturated.
[06:24] [06:24] Samir: Any known regressions when using prefix cache with function-calling / tools? We use tool calling for DB lookups mid-session.
[06:30] Carlos: Good call — tool calls that mutate context can invalidate cached prefixes; we support per-session invalidation markers. The Console can flag sequences that include tool calls and reduce effective cache hit estimates accordingly.
[06:40] Devon: Let's talk numbers for a pilot. If we run a four-week pilot on Hosted with Optimize config A vs Dedicated small pool, what's expected variance?
[06:48] Carlos: In general hosted is simplest and you'll see faster time-to-value; Dedicated gives better predictable P95 at scale and lower unit cost if you commit. For your traffic we'd estimate hosted pilot cost $6k/month for our simulated load, Dedicated reserve ~ $4.2k/month equivalent assuming 60% utilization. We'll put exact math in the CSV.
[07:06] Aisha: What about encryption for cache? We need KMS integration and audit logs for reads/writes.
[07:12] Maya: We'll include audit log examples. Dedicated & Private support bring-your-own KMS and HSM. Hosted can be configured with customer-managed keys in some enterprise packages.
[07:22] [07:22] Carlos: Ok I'm going to run QuickBench live with a small synthetic trace. (pause) The bench shows baseline decode time per request 28ms, queueing adds 60ms at your current concurrency, giving that 120ms P95. With prefix hits at 70% decode drops to 16ms and queueing effect halves, P95 ~ 70–80ms.
[07:46] Priya: Do you have an offline export we can review? The Optimize tab CSV you mentioned?
[07:50] Carlos: Yes it's the 'cost-sim CSV' export. It includes per-scenario parameters and per-token cost math. I'll attach it after the call.
[07:58] Devon: One last security angle — do cached prefixes travel to object storage that we've to approve? We want to avoid any accidental egress.
[08:04] Maya: Good note. For Dedicated/Private, storage can be VPC-only, and egress controls are supported. We'll document the exact flow.
[08:14] [08:14] Aisha: Ok, this was useful. For next steps, we'll send a sanitized 7-day trace and pick a pilot start date. Also want a short risks doc on cache invalidation & tool-calls.
[08:26] Maya: Great. Recap next steps: Maya to share cost CSV and kernel-selection doc; Carlos to run QuickBench when trace is available; Nova to provide trace and SLOs. We'll aim for pilot plan next week.
[08:40] Devon: Quick note — can you include a scenario with model quantization (int8) vs bf16? We have concerns about quality.
[08:46] Carlos: Yep we can include a quality vs cost delta, and we'll flag recommended eval prompts to check hallucination/regression.
[08:54] Samir: Thanks all.
[08:56] June: Thanks, we'll follow up with the links: Console export, QuickBench instructions, KMS diagram.
[09:02] Aisha: Thanks everyone, that covers it.
[09:06] [END]
